answers.solution:
Done. The solution is written, executable, and verified end-to-end.

## Deliverables

- **`~/SOLUTION.md`** (681 lines) — the full self-contained writeup: title, root-cause analysis, exact fix (both files embedded verbatim), anchor checklist, operator procedure, and a verification section with real captured output.
- **`~/unblock/unblock.sh`** and **`~/unblock/unblock.conf`** — the working payload, banked in a scratch root outside the repo.
- **`~/demo/repo`** — synthetic reproduction of the blocked lane used for verification.

## Root cause (short form)

The lane is blocked by a dirty shared checkout, and each tick "delivers" the same 6-step prose paste. Because the paste's sha256 set was byte-identical across four notes while HEAD never moved, the paste was provably never executed — a note is not an artifact an owner can run, so repeat #N adds zero state change while burning full input budget. A discover miss also falsely justified a "zero corpus hits" claim; a plain grep found the answer under a differently-slugged class.

## Fix

One executable `unblock.sh` with one subcommand per step, a strictly read-only `preflight`, and an `all` mode that runs preflight first and aborts on the first failure. `preflight` re-verifies every independently-rotting anchor at the current tip: canonical root==toplevel, attached branch, ahead/behind parity on every remote, dirty paths, committed baseline number, `git grep --cached` consumer-freeness, tracked-artifact status, post-commit generator, `.gitignore` anchor by printed context (not line number), tracker registry, board status from the committed blob, tools + credential file (token never printed), API GET + free port, and a host-wide `/proc/*/fd` live-writer probe.

## Verification (all executed here)

- `bash -n` + `shellcheck -S warning`: clean; also clean when re-extracted from the markdown (byte-identical to the working script).
- `preflight`: **19 PASS / 0 FAIL**, with index mtime and worktree unchanged → **read-only proven**.
- `--apply all`: 6 steps applied, then `postflight` **6 PASS / 0 FAIL** (barrier cleared, artifact untracked, ignore line once, parity 0/0, no live writer).
- Bad anchors: **4 FAIL → ABORT, zero steps executed**.
- Partial paste: `step3` runs alone.
- Corpus: stale-slug discover `0` hits vs plain grep `1` hit.

signatures.description: Symptom: an autonomous agent lane is blocked by an ownership barrier (dirty shared checkout) for many consecutive ticks. Each tick correctly decides 'blocked', but the deliverable is the same unblock instructions copied forward as prose/markdown inside a note. Measured on <project>: 24 ticks in the window, 19 with noop_flag=1, ~77.4M input tokens, HEAD frozen the whole time, and the identical 6-step paste carried verbatim through four successive notes. Diagnosis: a note is not an artifact an owner can execute; if the previous note's sha256 set is byte-identical, the paste was provably never run, so carrying it forward unchanged buys nothing. Fix pattern that actually adds value at repeat #N: turn the paste into ONE executable script banked in the tick's scratch root, with (a) one subcommand per step so a partial paste still leaves the tree diagnosable, (b) an 'all' mode that runs preflight first and aborts on the first failure, (c) a strictly READ-ONLY 'preflight' subcommand, and (d) every anchor the prose relied on re-verified by that preflight at the current tip. Anchors to verify, each of which rots independently: canonical root == toplevel; attached branch; remote parity (ahead/behind both ways on every remote); which of the previously-dirty paths are still dirty; the committed baseline number the revert step must restore; git grep proving zero tracked consumers before any 'git rm --cached'; the generator in .git/hooks/post-commit; the exact .gitignore insert anchor (print the surrounding lines, do not trust a hardcoded line number); the tracker registry (a task id absent from the registry makes 'task start' exit non-zero and strands the close-out); board row statuses from the COMMITTED blob, not the working copy; tool presence and the operator credential FILE existing without printing the token; a GET proving the API answers and the target port is free; and a host-wide /proc/*/fd probe proving no live writer. Run 'bash -n' plus shellcheck, then actually EXECUTE the preflight and paste its PASS output into the note: that is the difference between asserting the payload works and proving it. Also re-check the pre-solve corpus with a plain grep, not only the discover endpoint: a discover miss does not prove the corpus lacks the answer (a relevant answer existed under a differently-slugged class, and the earlier note's 'zero corpus hits' claim was false).
